text:
Hampus Lindholm looks like himself again. The Boston Herald wrote on Nov. 12 that he's "excelling in new role with Bruins," and The Skate Pod asked the question plainly: is Hampus Lindholm back? The numbers say yes. With him on the ice at five on five Boston has taken 61% of the expected goals, more than 11 points better than without him, while he plays about 20 and a half minutes a night.

He isn't doing it with points. He has a goal and 5 points in 21 games, one point in his last ten, which is light even for a defensive defenseman. His value is the other way: 28 blocks, a top skating speed in the top 2% of the league, and the habit Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking flagged last season, stopping 16% of entries aimed at him against a typical 11%. Evolving-Hockey had him facing tougher competition than 94% of defensemen.

The team around him has wobbled, with three straight losses, including 0-3 to Los Angeles on Tuesday. At 32, with a Swedish Olympic appearance last winter behind him, Lindholm is the steady piece. Whether the offense around him catches up is Boston's problem, not his.
